title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters in event group chat
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, prerequisites and external-presenter access match Microsoft's notice, and the documented controls and licensing background check out. One sentence should repeat the condition on access to earlier messages rather than imply that every existing message is visible.

claims.where: title; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Event group chat is the private coordination chat for organisers, co-organisers and presenters in an event or structured meeting.
claims.quote: Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support presenters from outside the hosting tenant in event group chat.
claims.quote: This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The events planning page lists No control for admins over event group chat in events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: Event group chat (organizers, co-organizers, and presenters) | No control. | Can chat with presenters and co-organizers. Attendees don't use this chat during events.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The printed Teams admin center route reaches the organisation's specific-domain allow-list control.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Users > External access. ... Next to Teams and Skype for Business users in external organizations, choose Allow only specific external domains. ... Select Add external domains.

claims.claim: Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowFederatedUsers $true enables the tenant federation master switch.
claims.quote: When set to True (the default value) users will be potentially allowed to communicate with users from other domains. ... the AllowFederatedUsers property serves as a master switch that globally enables or disables federation across the Tenant

claims.claim: Users > External access > Policies > policy > Manage external domains for this policy reaches the federation setting.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Users > External access. ... Select the Policies tab. ... Click to add a policy or modify an existing one. ... Turn on Manage external domains for this policy to allow federation in the policy.

claims.claim: Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $true turns on federation in the external access policy.
claims.quote: Turn on the external domain management for the external access policy: ... Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $True

claims.claim: Meetings > Events policies > policy > Verify external presenters before joining an event reaches join verification.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... In the Verify external presenters before joining an event dropdown list, select Yes verify accounts or No verification needed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires join verification.
claims.quote: To require external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP

claims.where: controls[3].ui and .api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No separately documented tenant UI or automation switch controls external presenters in event group chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external presenters event group chat admin disable PowerShell policy green room; "event group chat" "external presenters" default enabled admin switch. Opened plan-events, manage-event-chat and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; no separate switch found.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center External Collaboration left-rail section contains the existing External access page.
claims.quote: The External Collaboration section in the Teams Admin Center (TAC) left rail provides a unified location to manage all external collaboration settings. ... External access: This is the existing page to manage configuration of federation and communication with external domains

claims.claim: The default external access policy is labelled Org-wide default settings.
claims.quote: In the list of policies, select the Org-wide default settings.

claims.claim: Organisation external access settings can override external access policies.
claims.quote: Your organization's external access settings can override external access policies.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the policy as preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The existing event group chat for events optimised for large audiences is available before, during and after the event.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.claim: For events optimised for large audiences, event group chat is separate from attendee chat.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The presenter's stored tenantId changes from the organiser's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.
claims.quote: The presenter's stored tenantId also changes from the organizer's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The change adds a cross-tenant chat path between the organiser's tenant and external presenters.
claims.quote: We are adding a new cross-tenant chat path between the organizer's tenant and external presenters.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Both tenants must allow external access for this cross-tenant path.
claims.quote: Both tenants must allow external access.

claims.claim: The notice says the change stores no new customer data.
claims.quote: Does the change store new customer data? - No. Expected changes on the client will only correct the tenantId to the external federated presenter's own tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice places external presenters' messages under existing federated-chat handling.
claims.quote: External presenters' messages fall under existing federated-chat handling.

claims.claim: The described change is human presenter participation, not a described agent or automated action.
claims.quote: External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn requires both an organisation setting and a user policy to allow external access.
claims.quote: For a user to use external access, both the organization setting and a user policy must allow it.

claims.claim: The external access organisation settings and user policies are turned on by default.
claims.quote: Both the organization settings and user policies are turned on by default.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: A custom policy's Allow or block external domains value takes precedence over organisation domain settings.
claims.quote: Custom policy assigned to user: The value for Allow or block external domains setting in the custom policy takes precedence over organization settings.

claims.claim: The -AllowedDomains parameter takes an object created with New-CsEdgeAllowList or New-CsEdgeAllowAllKnownDomains, not a direct string.
claims.quote: Note that string values cannot be passed directly to the AllowedDomains parameter. Instead, you must create an object reference using the New-CsEdgeAllowList cmdlet or the New-CsEdgeAllowAllKnownDomains cmdlet

claims.claim: The -BlockedDomains parameter takes a List.
claims.quote: [-BlockedDomains <List>]

claims.claim: The events planning page lists No control for admins over the green room.
claims.quote: Green room | No control. | Can choose if green room is used for an event.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the event join-verification setting governs access to event group chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams ExternalPresenterJoinVerification event group chat access verification. Opened events-external-presenter-join-verification and manage-event-chat; the former governs joining events, without describing group-chat access.

claims.claim: Attendees do not use the event group chat.
claims.quote: Event group chat (organizers, co-organizers, and presenters) | No control. | Can chat with presenters and co-organizers. Attendees don't use this chat during events.

claims.claim: The supplied notice names no separate admin switch for the feature.
claims.quote: If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

claims.claim: The notice asks organisations wanting external-presenter chat to ensure external collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.
claims.quote: If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An external organisation's lack of reciprocal federation can prevent its presenters using the federated chat path.
claims.quote: We are adding a new cross-tenant chat path between the organizer's tenant and external presenters. Both tenants must allow external access.

claims.claim: Internal material already in the chat, such as run-of-show notes, is visible to external presenters under the preceding history condition.
claims.quote: External federated presenters can now read and post in the event group chat. That includes messages written before they joined, if the thread shows history.
claims.fix: Replace 'Anything internal already in that chat, such as run-of-show notes, is visible to them.' with 'Internal messages written before they joined, such as run-of-show notes, may be visible to them if the thread shows history.'
